question.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=5,$ since this is the number of components in each of the vectors of the null space. 

Also, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,|\,\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+2 & =5 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =5-2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
